title: Isaiah’s Burden
summary: Isaiah sees the burden of Babylon.

explicit_facts.text: Isaiah the son of Amoz saw the burden of Babylon.

unspecified_visual_details: Isaiah’s appearance and surroundings; how the burden is visually represented.

narration.text: The burden of Babylon

prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a specific event in Babylon; none is narrated here.

title: A Banner on the Mountain
summary: A command calls for a banner to be raised on a high mountain and a signal given to those who are to enter the gates of the nobles.

explicit_facts.text: The command is to lift a banner on a high mountain, raise the voice, shake the hand, and summon them to the gates of the nobles.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A banner can be shown raised on a high mountain; the commands may be conveyed as off-screen speech.
unspecified_visual_details: Who raises the banner and gives the signals; what the banner looks like; the identity of those summoned.

narration.text: Lift ye up a banner upon the high mountain
that they may go into the gates of the nobles.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse is a command, not a report that these actions occurred.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a named person or group carrying out the command as a narrated event.

title: The Called Ones
summary: The speaker declares that sanctified and mighty ones have been commanded and called.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker says the sanctified ones have been commanded and the mighty ones called.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The verse can be presented as off-screen speech over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance, identity, and location of the sanctified and mighty ones; whether they are visible.

narration.text: I have commanded my sanctified ones
I have also called my mighty ones

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse does not describe the called ones assembling or acting.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an army gathering as a present-tense event.

title: A Gathering in the Mountains
summary: Isaiah describes a tumultuous multitude in the mountains and hosts coming from a far country with weapons to destroy the land.

explicit_facts.text: A multitude like a great people makes a tumultuous noise in the mountains; kingdoms and nations are gathered, and the Lord of Hosts musters the hosts of battle.
They come from a far country, from the end of heaven, with weapons of the Lord’s indignation, to destroy the whole land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A gathered multitude and weapons may be shown in the mountains, without assigning them an identity beyond the text.
unspecified_visual_details: The multitude’s appearance, weapons, route, and exact location of the far country.

narration.text: a tumultuous noise of the kingdoms of nations gathered together
They come from a far country

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The wording describes a prophetic vision and must not be embellished with an unstated battle.
prohibited_inventions: Do not label the hosts as Medes here; the text names the Medes later.

title: The Day at Hand
summary: A warning declares that the day of the Lord is at hand and will come as destruction from the Almighty.

explicit_facts.text: The verse warns that the day of the Lord is at hand and will come as destruction from the Almighty.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Use off-screen speech over an unspecified setting.
unspecified_visual_details: Who is addressed and how the coming destruction looks.

narration.text: the day of the Lord is at hand
it shall come as a destruction from the Almighty.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: This is a warning, not a narrated depiction of destruction occurring.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show a specific destructive event not described in the verse.

title: Fear and Distress
summary: The people’s hands grow faint and hearts melt; they are afraid and distressed, looking at one another with faces like flames.

explicit_facts.text: All hands shall be faint and every man’s heart shall melt.
They shall be afraid, seized by pangs and sorrows, amazed at one another, and their faces shall be as flames.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People may be shown looking at one another in fear; the phrase “faces shall be as flames” is figurative and should not be rendered as literal fire.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities, exact expressions, clothing, and setting.

narration.text: And they shall be afraid
they shall be amazed one at another

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The similes concerning hearts melting and faces like flames are figures of speech.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal melting hearts or burning faces.

title: The Land Laid Desolate
summary: The prophecy describes the day of the Lord as a time of wrath that will lay the land desolate and remove its sinners.

explicit_facts.text: The day of the Lord comes with wrath and fierce anger to lay the land desolate and destroy its sinners from it.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Off-screen narration may accompany an unoccupied landscape, without depicting a specific destruction.
unspecified_visual_details: The land’s appearance and the manner of its desolation.

narration.text: to lay the land desolate
he shall destroy the sinners thereof out of it.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse predicts destruction; it does not describe a particular visible act.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage an unstated attack or depict gore.

title: The Lights Darkened
summary: The prophecy says the stars and constellations will withhold their light, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not shine.

explicit_facts.text: The stars and constellations shall not give their light; the sun shall be darkened in its going forth, and the moon shall not shine.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A darkened sky with the sun and moon present but not shining is supported.
unspecified_visual_details: The sky’s color and the precise arrangement or visibility of the heavenly bodies.

narration.text: the sun shall be darkened in his going forth
the moon shall not cause her light to shine.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes prophetic signs, not a specified time or location.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add an eclipse or other astronomical cause.

title: Pride Brought Low
summary: The speaker declares punishment for evil and iniquity, the end of the proud’s arrogance, and a man’s extraordinary preciousness.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker will punish the world for evil and the wicked for iniquity, cause the proud’s arrogance to cease, and lay down the haughtiness of the terrible.
A man will be made more precious than fine gold, even than the golden wedge of Ophir.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The declarations can be conveyed as off-screen speech; “more precious than fine gold” is figurative.
unspecified_visual_details: The man’s identity and appearance; any physical representation of the punishment.

narration.text: I will punish the world for evil
I will make a man more precious than fine gold

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The comparison to gold expresses preciousness and should not be literalized.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the man or invent an event that makes him precious.

title: Heavens Shaken
summary: The speaker declares that the heavens will be shaken and the earth will move from its place in the Lord’s fierce anger.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker will shake the heavens, and the earth shall move out of her place in the wrath of the Lord of Hosts.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A disturbed sky and earth may be depicted as prophetic imagery.
unspecified_visual_details: The appearance and scale of the shaking; any people or structures affected.

narration.text: I will shake the heavens
the earth shall remove out of her place

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse uses prophetic language; no specific visible mechanism is stated.
prohibited_inventions: Do not add an earthquake’s effects on people or buildings.

title: Flight to Their Own Lands
summary: The people scatter like chased animals, each turning to their own people and fleeing to their own land.

explicit_facts.text: They shall be like a chased roe and a sheep no one takes up; each shall turn to their own people and flee to their own land.

reasonable_visual_inferences: People fleeing in different directions is supported; the animal comparisons are figurative.
unspecified_visual_details: The people’s identities, destinations, and the landscape.

narration.text: they shall every man turn to his own people
and flee every one into his own land.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The chased roe and sheep are similes, not literal animals in the action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict an animal chase as the event.

title: The Proud Fall
summary: The prophecy says the proud will be thrust through and those joined to the wicked will fall by the sword.

explicit_facts.text: Every proud person shall be thrust through; everyone joined to the wicked shall fall by the sword.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The verse permits showing the stated physical action without gore.
unspecified_visual_details: Who carries out the action, where it occurs, and the people’s identities.

narration.text: Every one that is proud shall be thrust through
every one that is joined to the wicked shall fall by the sword.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes violence in a prophecy; depict action without wounds, blood, or severed body parts.
prohibited_inventions: Do not name attackers or add tactical details or gore.

title: The Medes Stirred Up
summary: The verses foretell violence against children, young men, and wives, the spoiling of houses, and the stirring up of the Medes against unnamed people. They say the Medes will not value silver or gold.
characters: Unnamed people referred to in the prophecy

explicit_facts.text: The verse foretells children dashed to pieces before others' eyes, houses spoiled, and wives ravished.
The speaker says the Medes will be stirred up against unnamed people and will not regard or delight in silver and gold.
The verse foretells that bows will dash young men to pieces and that children will not be spared.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Bows may be shown without depicting their use or the foretold violence as occurring now.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, timing, and appearance of the people are not specified in these verses.
The identity of the people opposed by the Medes is not stated in these verses.

narration.text: Their houses shall be spoiled
Behold, I will stir up the Medes against them
their eyes shall not spare children.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic statements; do not stage the foretold acts as events occurring in the scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the unnamed target as Babylon.
Do not depict sexual assault, wounds, blood, or severed body parts.
Do not add dialogue, motives, identities, or an appearance for the speaker.

title: Babylon Overthrown
summary: Babylon, described as the glory and beauty of kingdoms, will become as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

explicit_facts.text: Babylon, glory of kingdoms and beauty of the Chaldees’ excellency, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Babylon may be shown as a city under a prophetic comparison to its overthrow.
unspecified_visual_details: What the overthrow looked like and the city’s precise appearance.

narration.text: Babylon, the glory of kingdoms
shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Sodom and Gomorrah are referenced as a comparison, not as present characters or a separate scene.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Sodom and Gomorrah or invent specific details of Babylon’s overthrow.

title: Babylon Uninhabited
summary: Babylon will remain uninhabited; no Arabian will pitch a tent there, and no shepherd will make a fold there.

explicit_facts.text: Babylon will never be inhabited; no Arabian will pitch a tent there, and no shepherd will make a fold there.

reasonable_visual_inferences: An uninhabited landscape with no tent or shepherd’s fold is supported.
unspecified_visual_details: The city’s condition and the surrounding terrain.

narration.text: It shall never be inhabited
neither shall the shepherds make their fold there.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse describes a future state, not a present arrival or departure.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show Arabians or shepherds arriving or leaving.

title: Prophecy of Desolate Houses
summary: The verses foretell beasts inhabiting houses, owls dwelling there, satyrs dancing, and beasts and dragons crying in houses and palaces. They also foretell an approaching end, destruction, mercy for a people, and the perishing of the wicked.

explicit_facts.text: Wild beasts of the desert shall lie there; houses shall be full of doleful creatures; owls shall dwell there; and satyrs shall dance there.
Wild beasts of the islands shall cry in desolate houses, and dragons in pleasant palaces; her time is near and her day shall not be prolonged.
An unidentified first-person voice says it will destroy her speedily, be merciful to its people, and that the wicked shall perish.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Desolate houses can be shown as unoccupied by people, without depicting the prophecy as an event already occurring.
unspecified_visual_details: The identity of the first-person voice and of “her.”
The appearance or literal nature of satyrs and dragons.
The architecture, geographic setting, and manner of destruction.

narration.text: and owls shall dwell there, and satyrs shall dance there.
And the wild beasts of the islands shall cry in their desolate houses, and dragons in their pleasant palaces;
For I will destroy her speedily; yea, for I will be merciful unto my people, but the wicked shall perish.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are prophetic statements, not a narrated present-tense occurrence. The verses do not identify the first-person voice or establish a concrete appearance for satyrs or dragons.
prohibited_inventions: Do not identify the first-person voice or “her” as Babylon.
Do not depict satyrs or dragons as literal beings with invented designs.
Do not show destruction, mercy, or the perishing of the wicked as separate visible events.
